claims.statement: Four named RQ queues: webhook_high (worker-chatbot ×2), persistence_low (worker-persistence ×1), ingest (worker-ingest ×1), followup (worker-followup ×1). Replica counts are intentional: 2 chatbot for burst handling, 1 each for throughput-bound work on the 2-vCPU droplet.

register_unique_tick fixes a ~12× duplicate-tick bug: rq-scheduler's random-id scheduling stacked new jobs on every boot. The fix cancels all existing jobs targeting func, then registers with stable id 'vfic-tick-{func.__name__}'. register_unique_cron_tick does the same for wall-clock-pinned cron schedules.

Five registered ticks: proactive follow-up (1800s), reconcile sweep (60s), outbound dispatch (60s), decision trace retention (86400s), single-page external-source sync (cron '0 20 * * *' = 03:00 ICT). Each uses register_unique_tick or register_unique_cron_tick. Failure to register is non-fatal.

Reconcile sweep is the primary reliability guarantee: ~60s scan + 120s grace ≈ 3-4 min total recovery. Non-reentrancy via Redis SETNX lock (300s TTL). Classifies candidates: stale_pending, unanswered_inbound, stale_lock_breakable, stale_send_unknown, skipped_locked.

reconcile_grace_seconds (120s) MUST exceed chat_turn_job_timeout (60s): a candidate only surfaces after RQ has killed the job, so a stale-heartbeat lock is always a dead worker, never a live turn. A completed turn (sent/suppressed) leaves BOT/SENT or BOT/SUPPRESSED as newest message → excluded.

async_runner.run_async runs awaitables on a process-local event loop reused across jobs. _shutdown_loop (atexit) drains pending tasks (5s deadline), disposes LLM client cache, database engines, and HTTP clients. Each resource cleanup is isolated — one failure does not block the next.

Redis observability counters: reconcile_re_enqueues_total, reconcile_stale_pending_total, reconcile_unanswered_inbound_total, reconcile_skipped_locked_total, reconcile_enqueue_failed_total, reconcile_unknown_send_outcome, reconcile_stale_lock_broken, reconcile_unanswered_gauge. All read by GET /metrics.
